before.title: Stress-energy tensor, force density and local balance on flat spacetime
before.statement: Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, and let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be a nonempty open set. (a) A \emph{stress-energy tensor} on $\Omega$ of class $C^k$, $k\ge1$, is a $C^k$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field $T$ on $\Omega$ in the sense of [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]: at every $p$, $T(p):V^*\times V^*\to\mathbb R$ is bilinear and symmetric, so its inertial components satisfy $T^{ab}=T^{ba}$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii)). (b) In the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] with length coordinates $x^0=ct$, the components $T^{ab}$ have the unit joule per cubic metre; the frame components are read as energy density ($T^{00}$), energy flux and momentum density ($T^{0i}=T^{i0}$) and stress ($T^{ij}$). This clause fixes a unit and a reading convention only; it asserts no measurement, no matter model and no dynamics. (c) The \emph{four-force density} of $T$ is the $C^{k-1}$ field with inertial components $f^b:=\partial_aT^{ab}$, where $\partial_a$ are the coordinate partial derivatives of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. By [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iv) the components $\partial_aT^{ab}$ transform as a vector, so $f$ is a well-defined vector field on $\Omega$, independent of the inertial chart. One says that $T$ is \emph{locally conserved}, or \emph{balanced}, on $\Omega$ when $f=0$ on $\Omega$, and that $T$ is balanced against the four-force density $f$ when $\partial_aT^{ab}=f^b$. (d) The definition asserts no conservation of any prescribed symmetric field $T$: whether a given $T$ is conserved, whether it arises from an action or a matter model, and whether any of its integrals over a slice converges are separate hypotheses stated elsewhere. No choice principle is used.
before.strategy: Definition item fixing the class of fields, the component readings and the balance terminology. Obligations: (i) $T^{ab}=T^{ba}$ is chart-independent because $T$ is a symmetric bilinear form and the component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii) is linear in the tensor; (ii) $\partial_aT^{ab}$ is a $(1,0)$-component family under an affine change of inertial chart by clause (iv) of the same theorem, since the transition matrix is constant; (iii) the unit statement is a convention imported from [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] extended to the density components, and carries no mathematical content; (iv) no positivity, symmetry of the integral representation, conservation or dynamics is asserted. No choice principle is used.

after.title: Stress-energy tensor, force density and local balance on flat spacetime
after.statement: Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, and let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be a nonempty open set. (a) A \emph{stress-energy tensor} on $\Omega$ of class $C^k$, $k\ge0$ (with $C^0$ meaning continuous), is a $C^k$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field $T$ on $\Omega$ in the sense of [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]: at every $p$, $T(p):V^*\times V^*\to\mathbb R$ is bilinear and symmetric, so its inertial components satisfy $T^{ab}=T^{ba}$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii)). (b) Fix the positive numerical constant $c$ and, in each inertial chart, define the component families $\varepsilon_x:=T^{00}$, $\pi_x^i:=T^{0i}/c=T^{i0}/c$ and $S_x^{ij}:=T^{ij}$. These are numerical component and scaling conventions; their transformation is inherited from $T$. No physical units or measurement interpretation form part of this mathematical definition. (c) When $k\ge1$, the \emph{four-force density} of $T$ is the $C^{k-1}$ field with inertial components $f^b:=\partial_aT^{ab}$, where $\partial_a$ are the coordinate partial derivatives of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. By [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iv) the components $\partial_aT^{ab}$ transform as a vector, so $f$ is a well-defined vector field on $\Omega$, independent of the inertial chart. For $k\ge1$, one says that $T$ is \emph{locally conserved}, or \emph{balanced}, on $\Omega$ when $f=0$ on $\Omega$, and that $T$ is balanced against the four-force density $f$ when $\partial_aT^{ab}=f^b$. (d) The definition asserts no conservation of any prescribed symmetric field $T$: whether a given $T$ is conserved, whether it arises from an action or a matter model, and whether any of its integrals over a slice converges are separate hypotheses stated elsewhere. No choice principle is used. For a merely continuous tensor ($k=0$), the component conventions and pointwise contractions are defined, while divergence, four-force density and the balance terminology in (c) require the additional $C^1$ hypothesis; no derivative of a merely continuous field is asserted.
after.strategy: Definition of symmetric C^k type-(2,0) fields for k>=0, and of their divergence only for k>=1, with purely numerical component conventions. Symmetry is chart-independent by the rank-two tensor transformation law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]], clause (iii). For k>=1, under an affine inertial transition xprime=Lambda x+a the constant inverse Jacobian in partialprime_a cancels the first Lambda factor in Tprime^{ab}; hence partialprime_a Tprime^{ab}=Lambda^b_d partial_c T^{cd}, clause (iv). This proves chart-independence of the divergence field. The constants and component families in (b) are numerical definitions, not assertions of measured energy or momentum. No conservation, positivity, matter model, slice convergence or choice principle is asserted. The C0 case is well-defined by the existing tensor-field supplier, which permits k=0; the rank-two component law and symmetry use finite linear evaluation and no derivative of T. The observer decomposition expands delta=h-n tensor n pointwise, so its original continuous-T scope and all contraction/uniqueness conclusions are retained. The C1 and higher cases keep exactly the original divergence and balance claims.

before.title: Compact-support variation: the fundamental lemma, integration by parts and differentiation under the integral sign
before.statement: Work in an inertial chart $x$ of the affine Minkowski model, identifying a nonempty open $\Omega\subseteq A$ with its image in $\mathbb R^4$; all integrals are Riemann (Darboux) integrals. (a) If $g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and $\int_\Omega g\,\psi\,d^4x=0$ for every smooth compactly supported $\psi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, then $g=0$ on $\Omega$. (b) If $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is $C^1$ and compactly supported and $g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is $C^1$, then for each $a$, $\int_\Omega(\partial_af)g\,d^4x=-\int_\Omega f(\partial_ag)\,d^4x$, provided $g$ is $C^1$ on $\Omega$ and the products are extended by zero outside $\operatorname{supp}f$. (c) If $F:(-s_0,s_0)\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is continuous with continuous $\partial_sF$ and there is a compact $K\Subset\Omega$ with $F(s,z)=0$ for $z\notin K$ and all $s$, then $s\mapsto\int_\Omega F(s,z)\,d^4z$ is $C^1$ on $(-s_0,s_0)$ with derivative $\int_\Omega\partial_sF(s,z)\,d^4z$. The lemma is choice-free and is stated for the exact Riemann integration theory on bounded rectangles; no distribution theory, no $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ hypothesis and no choice principle is used.
before.strategy: For (a), suppose $g(p_0)\ne0$; by continuity choose a closed axis-parallel box $Q\Subset\Omega$ centred at $p_0$ on which $|g|\ge c>0$, and a smooth bump $\psi$ with $\psi=1$ on a sub-box $Q'\Subset Q$ and support in $Q$ ([[lem-euclidean-bump-for-a-compact-set-inside-an-open-set]]); then $\int_\Omega g\psi\ge c\int_{Q'}\psi>0$ by monotonicity and the positivity of the integral of a nonnegative continuous function on a nondegenerate box ([[thm-multidimensional-integral-properties]], [[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]]), a contradiction. For (b), extend $fg$ by zero, let $R$ be a box containing its support, apply the fundamental theorem in the coordinate $x^a$ on each line and Fubini's theorem for continuous functions on rectangles ([[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]]) to conclude $\int_{\mathbb R^4}\partial_a(fg)=0$; expand $\partial_a(fg)$ by [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]. For (c), apply [[thm-differentiation-under-the-integral-sign-on-a-compact-rectangle]] on a rectangle containing $K$ with the continuous partial $\partial_sF$. No choice principle is used.

after.statement: Work in an inertial chart $x$ of the affine Minkowski model, identifying a nonempty open $\Omega\subseteq A$ with its image in $\mathbb R^4$; all integrals are Riemann (Darboux) integrals. after.strategy:
(a) Suppose g(p) is nonzero. Set sigma=+1 if g(p)>0 and sigma=-1 if g(p)<0. By continuity there is a closed nondegenerate box Q compactly inside Omega on which sigma*g>=a>0. Choose a smaller closed nondegenerate box Qprime in int(Q). Apply [[lem-euclidean-bump-for-a-compact-set-inside-an-open-set]] to Qprime inside int(Q) to obtain a smooth bump rho with 0<=rho<=1, rho=1 on Qprime and support inside int(Q). Its finite-ball construction gives compact support. Use the signed test psi=sigma*rho. Its integral satisfies integral g*psi=integral (sigma*g)*rho >=a*vol(Qprime)>0, contrary to the hypothesis. Both signs of g(p) are thereby covered.
(b) The products fg, f partial_a g, and g partial_a f have compact support inside Omega. Their extensions by zero are respectively C1 and continuous on R4: near every point outside Omega they vanish on a neighbourhood, because supp(f) is a compact subset of Omega. Choose a bounding rectangle with this support in its interior. On each coordinate line the integral of partial_a(fg) is zero by FTC, since fg vanishes at the endpoints. Apply [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]] repeatedly to the continuous functions, and expand the product derivative to obtain the displayed integration-by-parts identity.
(c) Extend F and partial_s F by zero outside Omega. Since the common support K is compactly inside Omega, both extensions are continuous on each compact parameter interval times a bounding rectangle, and differentiation in s gives the extended partial_s F. The imported [[thm-differentiation-under-the-integral-sign-on-a-compact-rectangle]] has a one-spatial-variable public interface; apply it four times to the iterated coordinate integrals, using Fubini for continuous functions at each stage. Continuity of each integrated derivative follows from uniform continuity on the compact product and the bound |integral u|<=vol(R)*sup|u|. This proves C1 parameter dependence on each compact subinterval of (-s0,s0), hence everywhere there. The compactly supported integral does not depend on its bounding rectangle by [[lem-compactly-supported-riemann-integral-is-well-defined]]. All choices are finite; no AC or countable choice is used.

before.title: First variation of the scalar-field action and the Euler-Lagrange equation
before.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be a nonempty open set with an inertial chart $x$, let $K>0$ (joule per metre), let $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be smooth (values in inverse square metres) and let $\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth real scalar field ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]). For every smooth compactly supported $h:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ define the first variation $$\delta S(\varphi)[h]:=-\frac{K}{c}\int_\Omega\Big(\eta^{ab}\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_bh+V'(\varphi)h\Big)\,d^4x,$$ a finite Riemann integral by compact support of $h$ ([[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]\,(c)). Then (a) $\delta S(\varphi)[h]=\dfrac{K}{c}\int_\Omega\big(\Box\varphi-V'(\varphi)\big)h\,d^4x$, where $\Box\varphi:=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b\varphi$; (b) $\delta S(\varphi)[h]=0$ for every such $h$ if and only if $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ on $\Omega$. The equation in (b) is called the scalar-field equation of this model. The statement is the first variation of the action on compactly supported variations; it asserts nothing about convergence of $S$ on unbounded domains, no boundary term, no dynamics beyond the equivalence in (b) and no empirical fact. No choice principle is used.
before.strategy: Expand the first variation: the derivative term is $-\frac{K}{c}\int\eta^{ab}\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_bh$; integrate by parts in the coordinate $x^b$ using [[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]\,(b) to move $\partial_b$ onto $\eta^{ab}\partial_a\varphi$, and use $\eta^{ab}\partial_b\partial_a\varphi=\Box\varphi$ (relabeling and [[thm-young-mixed-partial-theorem]]). This proves (a). For (b), if $\Box\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$ then $\delta S=0$; conversely, the continuous function $g:=\Box\varphi-V'(\varphi)$ satisfies $\int g h=0$ for every smooth compactly supported $h$, so $g=0$ by [[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]\,(a). Sources: the displayed action and its variation are the flat restriction of (4.42)-(4.43) of the cited Tong text; the argument is standard. No choice principle is used.

Its integrand has support in $\operatorname{supp}h$, so it is defined for every real $s$ even when either background action diverges; $S_h\prime(0)=\delta S(\varphi)[h]$.

Mixed partial symmetry gives the displayed Box formula. If the residual is zero, stationarity follows. Conversely stationarity against every compactly supported h makes the continuous residual vanish by clause (a), including both signs. Neither a full-domain background action nor a boundary condition is used. This is the compact-support flat specialization of Tong (4.42)-(4.43) and its equation-of-motion calculation, with the relative functional made explicit; no choice principle is used.

u}(s):=\eta_{\mu
u}+s\,h_{\mu
u}$ is nondegenerate with negative determinant on $\operatorname{supp}h$ (such $s_0>0$ exists) set $$\mathcal A(s):=- rac{K}{c}\int_\Omega\Big(	frac12 g^{ab}(s)\,\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_b\varphi+V(\varphi)\Big)\sqrt{-\det g(s)}\,d^4x .$$ (a) $\mathcal A$ is differentiable at $0$ and $$ rac{d\mathcal A}{ds}(0)=+ rac{1}{2c}\int_\Omega T^{ab}h_{ab}\,d^4x,\qquad T^{ab}:=K\Big(\partial^a\varphi\,\partial^b\varphi-\eta^{ab} ig(	frac12\partial_c\varphi\,\partial^c\varphi+V(\varphi) ig)\Big),$$ where indices are moved with $\eta$. (b) $T$ is the unique continuous symmetric $(2,0)$ tensor field on $\Omega$ whose pairing against every compactly supported smooth symmetric variation $h$ equals $+(2c) rac{d\mathcal A}{ds}(0)$, i.e. $\int_\Omega T^{ab}h_{ab}\,d^4x=2c\, rac{d\mathcal A}{ds}(0)$; it is symmetric and its components have the unit joule per cubic metre. It is called the \emph{Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the scalar-field action}. after.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be any nonempty open set with inertial chart $x$, let $c,K>0$ be numerical constants, and let $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ and $\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. For each smooth symmetric $(0,2)$ tensor $h$ with compact support, set $g_{ab}(s)=\eta_{ab}+s h_{ab}$. Choose $s_0>0$ so that these matrices are nondegenerate with negative determinant for $|s|<s_0$; outside $\operatorname{supp}h$ they equal $\eta$. (a) $\mathcal A_h$ is differentiable at $0$ and $$\mathcal A_h\prime(0)=\frac1{2c}\int_\Omega T^{ab}h_{ab}\,d^4x,\qquad T^{ab}:=K[\partial^a\varphi\partial^b\varphi-\eta^{ab}(\tfrac12\partial_d\varphi\partial^d\varphi+V(\varphi))],$$ with indices raised by $\eta$. (b) $T$ is smooth and symmetric, and is the unique continuous symmetric $(2,0)$ field for which $\int_\Omega T^{ab}h_{ab}\,d^4x=2c\mathcal A_h\prime(0)$ for every such $h$. It is called the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of this scalar-field density. (c) The result holds on unrestricted open $\Omega$, uses only compactly supported metric variations, and imposes no convergence or boundary condition at infinity. If the full background action happens to exist, the relative action is its variation difference and gives the same derivative. No choice principle is used.

On the compact support of h its entries are bounded. The determinant is a polynomial in s with continuous coefficients, and det(eta)=-1; compactness supplies a uniform s0 for which det(g)<0. consumer_baseline.title: Stress balance and finite flux on closed boxes
consumer_baseline.statement: Let $x$ be an inertial chart of the affine Minkowski model with coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, let $B:=\prod_{a=0}^{3}[c_a,d_a]$ with $c_a<d_a$ be a closed axis-parallel box, and let $T$ be a $C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field on an open neighbourhood of $B$; put $f^b:=\partial_aT^{ab}$ (continuous on $B$) as in [[def-sr-stress-energy-tensor-and-force-density]]. (a) (Box identity.) For each $b$, with $F_a^+:=\{x\in B:x^a=d_a\}$, $F_a^-:=\{x\in B:x^a=c_a\}$ and each face integral the Riemann integral over the remaining three coordinates, $$\int_B f^b\,d^4x=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\Big(\int_{F_a^+}T^{ab}\,d^3x-\int_{F_a^-}T^{ab}\,d^3x\Big).$$ (b) (Slice balance.) Write $K:=\prod_{i=1}^{3}[c_i,d_i]$ and, for $s\in[c_0,d_0]$, $Q^b(s):=\int_K T^{0b}(s,x)\,d^3x$; this is finite and continuous in $s$. For $c_0\le s_1<s_2\le d_0$, $$Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)=\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K} f^b\,d^4x-\sum_{i=1}^{3}\Big(\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^+}T^{ib}\,d^3x-\int_{[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^-}T^{ib}\,d^3x\Big),$$ where $K_i^\pm$ are the two faces $x^i=d_i$, $x^i=c_i$ of $K$. (c) (Finite-flux conservation.) If $f=0$ on $[s_1,s_2]\times K$ and $T^{ib}=0$ on the side faces $[s_1,s_2]\times K_i^\pm$ for $i=1,2,3$, then $Q^b(s_1)=Q^b(s_2)$ for every $b$. The theorem concerns finite axis-parallel boxes in one inertial chart and is proved by the fundamental theorem of calculus. It does not assert a flux identity for arbitrary regions or hypersurfaces, does not assert that $Q^b$ transforms as a four-vector under a change of inertial chart, and asserts no conservation without the stated side-flux hypothesis; no noncompact or limiting statement is made. No choice principle is used.
consumer_baseline.strategy: For (a): for fixed values of the remaining coordinates, $x^a\mapsto T^{ab}$ is $C^1$ on $[c_a,d_a]$, so one-variable FTC ([[thm-ftc-second-part]]) gives $\int_{c_a}^{d_a}\partial_aT^{ab}\,dx^a=T^{ab}(d_a)-T^{ab}(c_a)$; integrate this identity over the remaining three coordinates and sum over $a$, using Fubini/iterated integration for continuous functions on rectangles ([[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]], [[cor-repeated-riemann-integrals-on-rectangles]]) and integrability of continuous functions on boxes ([[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]], [[def-multidimensional-darboux-integral]]). For (b): apply (a) to the sub-box $[s_1,s_2]\times K$ and identify the first and last faces with $Q^b(s_2)-Q^b(s_1)$ and the spatial faces with the displayed side-flux terms; continuity of $Q^b$ follows from continuity of $T^{0b}$ and the integral estimate ([[thm-multidimensional-integral-properties]]). (c) is immediate from (b). Source: this is the flat finite-box flux argument of S9 of the research supplier argument, the restricted version of Crowell 9.3.2-9.3.3 pp. 192-195, with the arbitrary-region argument declined. No choice principle is used.

consumer_baseline.title: Adopted continuum matter models and their evolution equations
consumer_baseline.statement: Adopt, on top of the flat spacetime postulates [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] and [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]], the SI conventions [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] and the particle premises [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]], the following classical continuum matter models on an open set $\Omega\subseteq A$: (i) Scalar field. A real smooth dimensionless field $\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, a smooth potential $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ with values in inverse square metres and a constant $K>0$ in joule per metre have the field equation $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ -- the Euler-Lagrange equation of the adopted action on compactly supported variations ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-euler-lagrange]]); the model's stress-energy tensor is the Hilbert tensor of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]]. (ii) Dust. A $C^1$ rest energy density $\rho>0$ (joule per cubic metre) and a $C^1$ future unit timelike field $n$ ($\eta(n,n)=-1$) satisfy $\partial_a(\rho n^a)=0$ and $n^a\partial_an^b=0$; the stress-energy tensor is $T=\rho\,n\otimes n$. (iii) Perfect fluid. $C^1$ fields $\varepsilon$ (energy density) and $P$ (pressure), both in joule per cubic metre, and a $C^1$ future unit timelike field $n$ satisfy the energy-balance and Euler equations of [[lem-sr-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]; an equation of state or evolution equation determining $P$ is part of the model and is not supplied by this postulate; the stress-energy tensor is $T=(\varepsilon+P)n\otimes n+P\eta$. (iv) Additivity. The total stress-energy tensor of a composite system is the sum of the stress-energy tensors of its constituents (tensor-field addition on $\Omega$). This postulate adopts model equations and tensor identifications only: it does not assert conservation of the tensors (that is derived from these equations in [[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]]), does not select any force law, interaction, equation of state, thermodynamic or dissipative behaviour, does not claim that these models exhaust physical matter, and contains no empirical premise, measurement or uncertainty statement.
consumer_baseline.strategy: Adopted physical premise; no proof obligation (the schema records postulates with formulation, scope and sources, not a deduction). The mathematical content used in the formulation is confined to the model equations and the displayed tensors; conservation is deliberately NOT part of this postulate. consumer_baseline.title: Adopted total stress-energy and isolation premise for integrated conservation
consumer_baseline.statement: Adopt as the boundary and isolation premise of the continuum framework: (i) Total tensor. In every conservation or integration statement of this framework the tensor used is the total stress-energy tensor of the system considered, including every constituent that carries energy-momentum -- matter, fields and supporting structures present in the region -- assembled by the additivity clause of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]]. (ii) Localisation. Whenever conservation of a slice four-momentum over a coordinate-time interval $[s_1,s_2]$ is asserted in an inertial chart, the model assumes that during that interval the total tensor is $C^1$ and symmetric on a neighbourhood of a closed box $[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K$, that its components satisfy the zero side-flux condition $T^{ib}=0$ on the spatial faces of the box for $i=1,2,3$, and that the slice integrals converge; equivalently, the system is isolated inside the chosen region for the chosen interval. (iii) Failure of isolation. If the side flux does not vanish, only the exact finite-flux balance of [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]] is asserted; no conservation of a slice integral is inferred and no limiting procedure at spatial infinity is adopted. (iv) Unmodelled matter. For a matter system not governed by one of the models of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]], conservation of its stress-energy tensor is not inferred; if used it must be adopted or derived separately. (v) Exclusion caution. Removing a constituent -- a support, a field or a container -- from the total tensor can make the side-flux condition fail; the premise concerns the total tensor of the system, not an arbitrary partial tensor. This premise is an idealisation of an isolated bounded system in flat spacetime; it is not a measurement and makes no apparatus, statistical or empirical claim.

consumer_baseline.statement: Under the matter premises of [[post-sr-matter-models-and-evolution]]: (a) If $\varphi$ is a smooth scalar field solving the adopted field equation $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ on $\Omega$, then the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the scalar-field action ([[lem-sr-scalar-field-hilbert-stress-energy]]) satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ on $\Omega$, in every inertial chart. consumer_baseline.title: Integrated four-momentum of an isolated system on finite slices
consumer_baseline.statement: Let $x$ be an inertial chart, let $\bar K$ be a closed spatial box and $s_1<s_2$, and let $T$ be the total stress-energy tensor of a system in the situation of [[post-sr-matter-isolation-and-total-stress-energy]]: $T$ is $C^1$ and symmetric on a neighbourhood of $[s_1,s_2]\times\bar K$, satisfies $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$ there (for the adopted models this is the conclusion of [[pthm-sr-local-stress-energy-conservation]]; for any other system it is an explicit premise), and satisfies the zero side-flux condition $T^{ib}=0$ on the spatial faces for $i=1,2,3$. consumer_baseline.title: Dust stress-energy in a boosted inertial frame
consumer_baseline.statement: In an inertial frame $x$ let dust at rest have rest energy density $\rho>0$, so $T^{ab}=\rho\,\delta^a_0\delta^b_0$; the only nonzero component is $T^{00}=\rho$. Consider the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] along the $x^1$ axis with parameter $\beta$, $|\beta|<1$, $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$: $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta x^1)$, $x'^1=\gamma(x^1-\beta x^0)$, $x'^2=x^2$, $x'^3=x^3$. By the component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]]\,(iii), $$T'^{00}=\gamma^2\rho,\quad T'^{01}=T'^{10}=-\gamma^2\beta\rho,\quad T'^{11}=\gamma^2\beta^2\rho,\quad T'^{22}=T'^{33}=0,$$ all remaining components zero; equivalently $T'=\rho\,n'\otimes n'$ where $n'$ is the image of $e_0$ under the boost, $n'^0=\gamma$, $n'^1=-\gamma\beta$, the future unit direction of the dust in the primed frame. The primed energy density $T'^{00}=\gamma^2\rho$ carries one factor of $\gamma$ from the increased energy of each dust particle and one from the contracted volume, as in the source computation. All primed components are constant, so $\partial'_aT'^{ab}=0$, consistently with [[lem-sr-dust-conservation-equivalence]]. The example is a component computation; it asserts no measurement and no dynamics.
consumer_baseline.strategy: Compute $T'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dT^{cd}$ with the boost matrix $\Lambda$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]]: only $T^{00}=\rho$ contributes, giving the displayed components; the identification $T'=\rho n'\otimes n'$ follows from $n'=\Lambda e_0$. Constancy and conservation are immediate. Source: Crowell Example 5 p. 185 and (1.106) of Carroll. No choice principle is used.

consumer_baseline.title: A dust solution with constant velocity and transverse density profile
consumer_baseline.statement: Let $|\beta|<1$, $\gamma=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, let $n$ be the constant field with inertial components $n^0=\gamma$, $n^1=\gamma\beta$, $n^2=n^3=0$ (so $\eta(n,n)=-1$), and let $\rho(t,x)=\rho_0(x^2,x^3)$ be a positive $C^1$ function of the transverse coordinates only. consumer_baseline.statement: In an inertial chart let $T^{ab}(x)=\rho(x^1)e_0^ae_0^b+P(x^1)e_1^ae_1^b$ with $\rho,P$ of class $C^1$ on an interval of $x^1$ (a static uniaxial stress field in the $e_1$ direction; $P<0$ is a tension). consumer_baseline.statement: In an inertial chart define the smooth symmetric field by $T^{00}=x^0$, $T^{01}=T^{10}=-x^1$, $T^{11}=x^0$ in the $(e_0,e_1)$ block and $0$ in all components involving $e_2$ or $e_3$. consumer_baseline.title: A prescribed covariant stress-energy tensor need not be conserved
consumer_baseline.statement: In an inertial chart let $\Omega$ be open and connected and let $F:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be $C^1$; define the smooth symmetric field $T^{ab}:=F\,\eta^{ab}$. The field $T=F\eta$ is not claimed to be the stress-energy tensor of any of the page's matter models.

consumer_baseline.title: First variation of the scalar-field action and the Euler-Lagrange equation
consumer_baseline.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be a nonempty open set with an inertial chart $x$, let $K>0$ (joule per metre), let $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be smooth (values in inverse square metres) and let $\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth real scalar field ([[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]]). For every smooth compactly supported $h:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ define the first variation $$\delta S(\varphi)[h]:=-\frac{K}{c}\int_\Omega\Big(\eta^{ab}\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_bh+V'(\varphi)h\Big)\,d^4x,$$ a finite Riemann integral by compact support of $h$ ([[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]\,(c)). Then (a) $\delta S(\varphi)[h]=\dfrac{K}{c}\int_\Omega\big(\Box\varphi-V'(\varphi)\big)h\,d^4x$, where $\Box\varphi:=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b\varphi$; (b) $\delta S(\varphi)[h]=0$ for every such $h$ if and only if $\Box\varphi=V'(\varphi)$ on $\Omega$. The equation in (b) is called the scalar-field equation of this model. The statement is the first variation of the action on compactly supported variations; it asserts nothing about convergence of $S$ on unbounded domains, no boundary term, no dynamics beyond the equivalence in (b) and no empirical fact. No choice principle is used.
consumer_baseline.strategy: Expand the first variation: the derivative term is $-\frac{K}{c}\int\eta^{ab}\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_bh$; integrate by parts in the coordinate $x^b$ using [[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]\,(b) to move $\partial_b$ onto $\eta^{ab}\partial_a\varphi$, and use $\eta^{ab}\partial_b\partial_a\varphi=\Box\varphi$ (relabeling and [[thm-young-mixed-partial-theorem]]). This proves (a). For (b), if $\Box\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$ then $\delta S=0$; conversely, the continuous function $g:=\Box\varphi-V'(\varphi)$ satisfies $\int g h=0$ for every smooth compactly supported $h$, so $g=0$ by [[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]\,(a). Sources: the displayed action and its variation are the flat restriction of (4.42)-(4.43) of the cited Tong text; the argument is standard. No choice principle is used.

consumer_baseline.title: Null plane-wave scalar field and its conserved stress-energy tensor
consumer_baseline.statement: Let $k\neq0$ be a null covector, $\eta^{ab}k_ak_b=0$, with $k^\sharp$ future, let $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be smooth, $\theta_0\in\mathbb R$, and let $\varphi(x):=f(k_ax^a+\theta_0)$ in an inertial chart; take $V\equiv0$ and $K>0$. Then $\varphi$ is a smooth scalar field, $\partial_a\varphi=f'(k_ax^a+\theta_0)k_a$ and $\Box\varphi=k^ak_af''(k_ax^a+\theta_0)=0$, so $\varphi$ solves the massless scalar-field equation of [[lem-sr-scalar-field-euler-lagrange]]. Its Hilbert stress-energy tensor is $$T^{ab}=Kf'(k_ax^a+\theta_0)^2\,k^ak^b,$$ symmetric, future-null directed, with $T^{ab}n_an_b=Kf'^2\,(k_an^a)^2\ge0$ for every future unit observer $n$, and conserved, $\partial_aT^{ab}=0$, by [[lem-sr-scalar-field-stress-divergence-identity]] evaluated on the solution $\Box\varphi=0$. In an inertial frame $T^{00}=Kf'^2(k^0)^2\ge0$. The example is an explicit conditional computation for the massless scalar model; it asserts no wave observation and no measurement.

The equation of motion holds because $k$ is null, and conservation follows from [[lem-sr-scalar-field-stress-divergence-identity]]. actual_read_suppliers.title: C^k tensor fields on affine Minkowski space and their inertial components
actual_read_suppliers.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space, regarded as the smooth 4-manifold with its inertial atlas (lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas), and let Omega be a nonempty open subset of A. Let r,s >= 0 be integers and let k be a nonnegative integer or k = infinity. Write T^{r,s}(V) for the real vector space of type-(r,s) tensors on V, i.e. of multilinear maps (V*)^r x V^s -> R (def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space, def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional), with the identification T_pA = V for every p in A (lem-tangent-space-of-affine-minkowski-space-is-v). A C^k type-(r,s) tensor field on Omega is a map T that assigns to each p in Omega a tensor T(p) in T^{r,s}(V) such that the map Omega -> T^{r,s}(V), p |-> T(p), is of class C^k as a map from the smooth manifold Omega into the finite-dimensional real vector space T^{r,s}(V) (with any norm; finite-dimensional real vector spaces are Banach spaces and all norms are equivalent). The components of T in the inertial chart x of a frame (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) are the functions T^{a_1...a_r}_{b_1...b_s}(p) := T(p)(e*^{a_1},...,e*^{a_r}, e_{b_1},...,e_{b_s}), where (e*^a) is the basis of V* dual to (e_a). Then T is C^k if and only if all its components in one (equivalently, every) inertial chart are C^k functions of x(p), because the identification above is linear; this equivalence is the elementary form of the component law proved in thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation. A type-(0,0) field is called a scalar field, a type-(1,0) field a vector field, and a type-(0,1) field a covector field.
actual_read_suppliers.strategy: A definition item. Its well-definedness rests on three supplied facts: the tangent spaces of the affine model are canonically identified with V (lem-tangent-space-of-affine-minkowski-space-is-v); the inertial charts form a smooth atlas, so 'C^k as a map on Omega' has a definite meaning (lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas, def-smooth-manifold, def-c-k-map-between-banach-spaces); and T^{r,s}(V) is a finite-dimensional real vector space carrying a canonical smooth structure, so the regularity of p |-> T(p) is a property of the map, not of a chosen chart. The component formula uses the dual basis of the frame's basis of V and the identification T_pA = V; the definition must state explicitly that components are frame-dependent arrays while T(p) is a frame-independent multilinear map, and that the component functions of a C^k field in an inertial chart are C^k (the converse direction is the component law). The equivalence asserted in the statement is proved through the constant linear transition matrices between two frames and their inverses, which are C^infinity; no derivative of the tensor field itself is used in this definition.

actual_read_suppliers.title: Transformation of tensor, covector, derivative and current components under affine Lorentz maps
actual_read_suppliers.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space, let x and x' be inertial charts whose transition is the affine map x'(p) = Lambda x(p) + b with linear part Lambda (a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix by lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz), and let Omega be an open subset of A. Let J: Omega -> V, k, and T be a C^k vector field, a C^k covector field and a C^k type-(r,s) tensor field on Omega in the sense of def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space, with components J^a, k_a and T^{a_1...a_r}_{b_1...b_s} in the chart x, and primed components in the chart x'. Then: (i) J'^a = Lambda^a_b J^b: a contravariant index gains the factor Lambda^a_b, i.e. components transform by multiplication with the transition matrix. (ii) k'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a k_b: a covariant index gains the factor (Lambda^{-1})^b_a. If theta(p) = k_a x^a(p) + theta_0 is an affine scalar function with constant covector k and constant theta_0, then theta(p) = k'_a x'^a(p) + theta'_0 with k' as above and theta'_0 := theta_0 - k'_a b^a, so the phase function is invariant when the constant term is transformed together with the covector. (iii) T'^{a_1...a_r}_{b_1...b_s} = Lambda^{a_1}_{c_1} ... Lambda^{a_r}_{c_r} (Lambda^{-1})^{d_1}_{b_1} ... (Lambda^{-1})^{d_s}_{b_s} T^{c_1...c_r}_{d_1...d_s}: every contravariant index gains a factor Lambda and every covariant index a factor Lambda^{-1}, and the law is consistent with the multilinear evaluation of T(p) after substituting the transformed basis. Every contraction of one contravariant with one covariant index is invariant, and the metric components satisfy eta'_{ab} = eta_{ab}. (iv) The coordinate partial derivatives satisfy partial'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a partial_b wherever the derivatives exist. Consequently the divergence of a vector field is invariant, partial'_a J'^a = partial_a J^a, and for a C^1 type-(2,0) field T one has partial'_a T'^{ab} = Lambda^b_c partial_a T^{ac}. (v) Alternating covariant tensor fields transform by the covariant law on each slot; the oriented volume form of the model satisfies epsilon'_{abcd} = epsilon_{abcd}, since det Lambda = +1, whereas a general Lorentz matrix with det = -1 changes its sign. (vi) Let J be a C^1 vector field with components (J^0,J^1,J^2,J^3) in an inertial chart, and write the spatial block as J_cov := (J^1,J^2,J^3) and denote by partial_i the spatial partial derivatives in the chart. Then the continuity equation partial_a J^a = 0 is equivalent to partial_0 J^0 + sum_i partial_i J^i = 0, and under the passive boost with parameter beta (Lambda = B(beta), Lambda^{-1} = B(-beta)) the components transform as J'^0 = gamma(J^0 - beta . J_cov), J'_cov = J_cov + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . J_cov) beta - gamma beta J^0. (vii) If U is a C^1 future timelike vector field and rho_0 a C^1 scalar field, then J := rho_0 U is a C^1 vector field and its first component satisfies J^0 = rho_0 U^0; writing rho := J^0 (the coordinate density in the chart) and u := U/U^0 (the coordinate velocity), one has rho = rho_0 u^0. Coordinate density and the scalar multiplier rho_0 are different objects: they agree only in charts in which u^0 = 1. Interpretation boundary: the identification of a physical charge-current with a vector field, and of rho with a measured charge density, is a model premise of the electromagnetic framework; this item is a statement about the transformation of components of specified fields and does not by itself assert that any physical current transforms as a vector.
actual_read_suppliers.strategy: Proof plan. (i) and (ii) are the definitions of components: for a vector field, J'(p) = sum_a J'^a(p) partial'_a|_p and partial'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a partial_b, so comparing coefficients with J = sum_b J^b partial_b gives J'^a = Lambda^a_b J^b; the covector transform is the dual statement k'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a k_b. The affine phase invariance in (ii) is the displayed substitution k_a x^a = k'_c x'^c - k'_c b^c. (iii) is the multilinear evaluation: writing T(p) on the transformed basis and using the definition of the components, each contravariant slot contributes Lambda and each covariant slot the inverse; the contraction claim follows from (Lambda^{-1})^a_b Lambda^b_c = delta^a_c, and eta'_{ab} = eta_{ab} is the matrix form of the defining Lorentz property of Lambda. (iv) is the chain rule for the transition x' = Lambda x + b: partial'_a = (partial x^c / partial x'^a) partial_c = (Lambda^{-1})^c_a partial_c; substituting into partial'_a J'^a and using (i) gives the invariance of the divergence, and the (2,0) case follows by the same substitution with the two contravariant factors. (v) An alternating covariant field is a covariant tensor field, so the slot-by-slot covariant law applies; for the volume form, which by def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form is the determinant of the coordinate matrix in an oriented frame, the transformation multiplies the determinant by det(Lambda^{-1}) = 1, and by det Lambda = -1 in the improper case. (vi) is the matrix multiplication of the boost matrix with the component vector; (vii) is the elementary computation J^0 = rho_0 U^0 = rho_0 (U^0/c) c... rather, with u := U/U^0 the identity rho = J^0 = rho_0 U^0 = rho_0 u^0 is immediate, and the last clause is the statement that u^0 = 1 characterizes the charts in which the coordinate density equals the scalar multiplier. The item must not claim that a physical current is a vector field: that adoption belongs to the electromagnetic model, and the final paragraph of the statement records the boundary. All computations are finite algebra and the chain rule for total derivatives.
